en: Itivuttaka 22:
Ekakanipāta,
Third Chapter (Tatiyavagga)
The *Mettasutta*.
Thus it was said by the Blessed One; so have I heard:
"Monks, do not be afraid of meritorious deeds."
“Bhikkhus, this is a designation for happiness—what is wished for, desired, dear, and agreeable—namely, meritorious deeds.
Indeed, bhikkhus, I recall experiencing for a long time the wished-for, desired, dear, and agreeable result of meritorious deeds performed in the past.
Having developed a mind of loving-kindness for seven years, I did not return to this world for seven aeons of dissolution and evolution.”
“Monks, when the aeon was contracting, I went to the Ābhassara realm;
when the aeon was expanding, I was reborn in an empty Brahma-mansion.
There, monks, I was Brahmā, the Great Brahmā, the conqueror, the unconquered, the all-seeing, the wielder of power.”
Furthermore, monks, thirty-six times I was Sakka, lord of the devas;
and many hundreds of times I was a wheel-turning monarch, righteous, a king of Dharma, conqueror of the four quarters, stabilizer of the land, and possessor of the seven treasures—
let alone the sovereignty over a single province.
Then, monks, this occurred to me:
“Of what deed of mine is this the fruit, of what deed is this the result, that I am now so powerful and so majestic?
Then, monks, this occurred to me:
“This is the fruit of three kinds of action, the result of three kinds of action, by which I am now so powerful and so majestic:
namely, giving, self-control, and restraint.
Thus the Blessed One spoke on this matter.
In this regard, it is said:
"One should train only in merit,
which has a long-term goal and results in happiness;"
One should cultivate generosity, righteous conduct,
and a mind of loving-kindness.
Having cultivated these qualities, [one attains the goal].
Three [are the causes] for the arising of happiness:
the wise person is reborn in a world that is free from harm and full of happiness.”
This matter too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The second [sutta].
